name: Tarngrisnir
body:
TARNGRISNIR
CR 9

This massive goat has a pair of lengthy curving horns, thick shaggy fur, and an intense wild-eyed gaze.

XP 6,400
N Large outsider (extraplanar)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 23, touch 11, flat-footed 21 (+2 Dex, +12 natural, –1 size)
hp 114 (12d10+48)
Fort +12, Ref +8, Will +11
Resist sonic 20

OFFENSE

Speed 80 ft., fly 80 ft. (good)
Melee bite +17 (1d8+6), gore +17 (2d6+6), 2 hooves +12 (1d6+3)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft. (10 ft. with bite and gore)
Special Attacks powerful charge (gore, 4d6+9), thunderous charge

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 15, Con 19, Int 4, Wis 12, Cha 12
Base Atk +12; CMB +19; CMD 31 (35 vs. trip)
Feats Endurance, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack, Run
Skills Fly +19, Intimidate +16, Perception +16
Languages Celestial (can’t speak)
SQ revive

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Revive (Su)

A tarngrisnir can be slaughtered and consumed.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold and temperate hills
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

However, performing a 4th level ritual at dawn (see Occult Adventures for more details) over a dead tarngrisnir’s skin and bones causes it to rise up whole again. The complete skin and all the bones must be present and undamaged, otherwise the tarngrisnir has matching injuries when it returns to life.

Thunderous Charge (Su)

When a tarngrisnir charges, the force of its hooves unleashes a rumbling wave of thunderous noise.

This deals 5d6 points of sonic damage to all creatures within 10 feet of the path of the charge (DC 20 Fortitude save for half damage). Creatures that fail this saving throw are also deafened for 2d6 rounds. The target of charge and any creatures within 10 feet of this target who fail their saving throws are also dazed for 1 round. Creatures riding a tarngrisnir, as well as those being drawn by one in a vehicle such as a chariot, are unaffected by this ability. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Tarngrisnirs (also called tanngnjóstr) are powerful storm?born goats that often serve as draft?beasts to powerful divine beings, capable of tirelessly bearing a rider, or drawing an immortal’s chariot, across land, sky, and sea. When a tarngrisnir runs, storm fire flickers on its breath, lightning sparks from the wheels of the chariot it pulls, and the noise of its hooves echoes like thunder.

Tarngrisnirs’ bodies possess a supernatural resilience: they can be killed, skinned, and even consumed, only to rise whole again when revived through a dawn ritual.

Their name translates to “teeth-snarler” or “teethgrinder”, highlighting their formidable predatory teeth and hinting at their carnivorous appetite. Although ferocious, tarngrisnirs are intensely loyal to those they accept as a master.
